lines.raw: **Ram** works at a tech startup in Kathmandu and has private health insurance: he pays the hospital himself, then claims the money back.

lines.raw: **Sita** is an accountant in Kathmandu who contributes to the Social Security Fund (SSF): she pays her share at an SSF-listed hospital and SSF pays the hospital the rest.

lines.raw: This course looks at that visit from the **clinic's** side: how the clinic made sure it got paid.

lines.raw: When Ram visits a private hospital, he usually pays at the **billing counter** before or right after he is seen.
lines.say: When Ram visits a private hospital, he usually pays at the billing counter before or right after he is seen.

lines.raw: The hospital has its money the same day.
lines.say: The hospital has its money the same day.

lines.raw: For the hospital, Ram's visit is simple: register him, record the services, print the bill, take the cash.
lines.say: For the hospital, Ram's visit is simple: register him, record the services, print the bill, take the cash.

lines.raw: Ram's insurer is Ram's problem, not the hospital's.

lines.raw: That chain of jobs, from registration to money in the bank, is what the US calls the **revenue cycle**.
lines.say: That chain of jobs, from registration to money in the bank, is what the U S calls the revenue cycle.

lines.raw: (SSF procedures change over time, so treat this as the general idea.).

lines.raw: The idea in one sentence.
lines.say: The idea in one sentence.

lines.raw: Simple definition.
lines.say: Simple definition.

lines.raw: **Revenue cycle management (RCM)** is everything a doctor's office or hospital does to get paid for care: from the moment a patient books a visit until every dollar is collected or written off.
lines.say: Revenue cycle management (R C M) is everything a doctor's office or hospital does to get paid for care: from the moment a patient books a visit until every dollar is collected or written off.

lines.raw: In the US: Why the US revenue cycle is long.
lines.say: In the U S: Why the U S revenue cycle is long.

lines.raw: Most US patients have insurance, so most of the money comes from an **insurer** (the payer), not the patient, and it arrives **weeks later**.
lines.say: Most U S patients have insurance, so most of the money comes from an insurer (the payer), not the patient, and it arrives weeks later.

lines.raw: A clinic may bill dozens of insurers, and each has its own plans, rules and forms.
lines.say: A clinic may bill dozens of insurers, and each has its own plans, rules and forms.

lines.raw: The patient pays a **share** (copay, deductible, coinsurance), sometimes at the visit and sometimes after the insurer has decided.
lines.say: The patient pays a share (copay, deductible, coinsurance), sometimes at the visit and sometimes after the insurer has decided.

lines.raw: Every step can go wrong: a typo at registration, a missing code, a missing approval.
lines.say: Every step can go wrong: a typo at registration, a missing code, a missing approval.

lines.raw: Each mistake delays or loses money.
lines.say: Each mistake delays or loses money.

lines.raw: Providers run this with a **billing office** (in hospitals often called **patient financial services**) or hire an outside **RCM company** to do it for them.
lines.say: Providers run this with a billing office (in hospitals often called patient financial services) or hire an outside R C M company to do it for them.

lines.raw: Three parts of the cycle.
lines.say: Three parts of the cycle.

lines.raw: Front end: before the visit.
lines.say: Front end: before the visit.

lines.raw: Scheduling, registration, checking insurance, getting approvals, estimating and collecting the patient's share.
lines.say: Scheduling, registration, checking insurance, getting approvals, estimating and collecting the patient's share.

lines.raw: Lesson 2.
lines.say: Lesson 2.

lines.raw: Mid cycle: during and after the visit.
lines.say: Mid cycle: during and after the visit.

lines.raw: Recording every service (charge capture), the price list, documentation and coding.
lines.say: Recording every service (charge capture), the price list, documentation and coding.

lines.raw: Lesson 3.
lines.say: Lesson 3.

lines.raw: Back end: getting the money in.
lines.say: Back end: getting the money in.

lines.raw: Building and sending claims, fixing rejections, following up, posting payments (lesson 4), working denials (lesson 5) and collecting from patients (lesson 6).
lines.say: Building and sending claims, fixing rejections, following up, posting payments (lesson 4), working denials (lesson 5) and collecting from patients (lesson 6).

lines.raw: Who does what.
lines.say: Who does what.

lines.raw: **Front end**. Main jobs: Book, register, verify insurance, collect copay. Usually done by: Schedulers, front desk, registration staff. Typical problem: Wrong insurance ID typed in.
lines.say: Front end. Main jobs: Book, register, verify insurance, collect copay. Usually done by: Schedulers, front desk, registration staff. Typical problem: Wrong insurance I D typed in.

lines.raw: **Mid cycle**. Main jobs: Capture charges, document, code. Usually done by: Doctors, nurses, medical coders. Typical problem: A test was done but never charged.
lines.say: Mid cycle. Main jobs: Capture charges, document, code. Usually done by: Doctors, nurses, medical coders. Typical problem: A test was done but never charged.

lines.raw: **Back end**. Main jobs: Send claims, follow up, post payments, appeal denials, bill patients. Usually done by: Billing staff, follow-up and denial teams. Typical problem: Claim denied and nobody notices for 90 days.
lines.say: Back end. Main jobs: Send claims, follow up, post payments, appeal denials, bill patients. Usually done by: Billing staff, follow-up and denial teams. Typical problem: Claim denied and nobody notices for 90 days.

lines.raw: Key words.
lines.say: Key words.

lines.raw: Charge.
lines.say: Charge.

lines.raw: The amount the provider records for a service, from its own price list.
lines.say: The amount the provider records for a service, from its own price list.

lines.raw: It is the starting point, not what the provider will actually be paid.
lines.say: It is the starting point, not what the provider will actually be paid.

lines.raw: Accounts receivable (AR).
lines.say: Accounts receivable (A R).

lines.raw: Money the provider is **owed but has not received yet**, from insurers and patients.
lines.say: Money the provider is owed but has not received yet, from insurers and patients.

lines.raw: Every charge enters AR and leaves it when it is paid, adjusted or written off.
lines.say: Every charge enters A R and leaves it when it is paid, adjusted or written off.

lines.raw: Guarantor.
lines.say: Guarantor.

lines.raw: The person responsible for paying the patient's share.
lines.say: The person responsible for paying the patient's share.

lines.raw: For an adult it is usually the patient; for a child, a parent.
lines.say: For an adult it is usually the patient; for a child, a parent.

lines.raw: Write-off (adjustment).
lines.say: Write-off (adjustment).

lines.raw: Taking an amount off the patient's account without collecting it, for example the insurer's contract discount.
lines.say: Taking an amount off the patient's account without collecting it, for example the insurer's contract discount.

lines.raw: Payer.
lines.say: Payer.

lines.raw: Whoever pays the claim: an insurer, Medicare, Medicaid or the patient.
lines.say: Whoever pays the claim: an insurer, Medicare, Medicaid or the patient.

lines.raw: Two sides of the same claim.
lines.say: Two sides of the same claim.

lines.raw: The **Claim Adjudication** course follows a claim **inside the insurer**: how it is checked and priced.
lines.say: The Claim Adjudication course follows a claim inside the insurer: how it is checked and priced.

lines.raw: RCM is the **provider's** side: preparing the claim so it passes those checks, and chasing the money when it does not.
lines.say: R C M is the provider's side: preparing the claim so it passes those checks, and chasing the money when it does not.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: **Revenue cycle management (RCM)** = everything a provider does to get paid, from booking to the final dollar.
lines.say: Revenue cycle management (R C M) = everything a provider does to get paid, from booking to the final dollar.

lines.raw: The cycle has three parts: **front end** (before the visit), **mid cycle** (charges and coding), **back end** (claims, payments, denials, patient bills).
lines.say: The cycle has three parts: front end (before the visit), mid cycle (charges and coding), back end (claims, payments, denials, patient bills).

lines.raw: **Accounts receivable (AR)** is money the provider is owed but has not yet received.
lines.say: Accounts receivable (A R) is money the provider is owed but has not yet received.

lines.raw: RCM is the provider's view; adjudication is the insurer's view of the same claim.
lines.say: R C M is the provider's view; adjudication is the insurer's view of the same claim.
